cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Call It a Fair Win
cards.instruction: Get them to recognize the result as deserved rather than accidental, gifted, or manipulated.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Say I earned the quiz trophy, not that the questions suited me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There were a lot of bird questions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. I spent six months learning birds. That's preparation with feathers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You were lucky they asked them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And the birds were lucky I was ready. Now call it earned.

mechanism: A takes authority over how B names the result and converts B explanations of luck or leniency into grounds for declaring A deserved merit.
confusable: Merely enjoying victory is confusable: B must question deservingness and A must actively seek a revised acknowledgment addressing that explanation.
comparison: Quiz preparation counters favorable-topic luck; race preparation claims merit from another runner shoe problem.
seedUse: Both exact cards and four canonical seeds read. Preserve actual contrary details and distinguish A argument from proven causes of winning.
